questions.question: The Begumpuri mosque was built during the reign of which of the following rulers of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Begumpuri Mosque: Muhammad Tughlaq
  • Detail: Located in Jahanpanah, the fourth city of Delhi, it served as the main congregational mosque for the city.

questions.question: Sun temple at Modhera was built by which of the following rulers?
questions.solution:
• Modhera Sun Temple: Raja Bhimdev I
  • Dynasty: Built by the Solanki king in 1026-27 CE. It is famous for its intricate carvings and the Surya Kund (stepwell).

questions.question: ‘Kabuli Bagh Mosque’ of Panipat was constructed by which Mughal ruler?
questions.solution:
• Kabuli Bagh Mosque: Babur
  • History: Built in 1527 to commemorate his victory over Ibrahim Lodi in the First Battle of Panipat.

questions.question: What did the rulers of Vijayanagara call themselves?
questions.solution:
• Vijayanagara Title: Raya
  • Examples: Famous rulers include Krishna Deva Raya and Deva Raya I.

questions.question: In Vrindavan, near Mathura, temples were constructed in architectural styles that were very similar to the Mughal palaces in ________.
questions.solution:
• Vrindavan Architecture: Fatehpur Sikri
  • Style: Red sandstone temples like the Govind Dev Temple (1590) utilized the trabeated construction common in Akbar's palaces.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad?
questions.option_1: It was built by Mughal prince Azam Shah.
questions.option_2: It is an imitation of the Taj Mahal due to its similar designs.
questions.option_3: It is the burial place of Aurangzeb's wife, Rabia-ud-Durrani.
questions.option_4: It is built completely with marble.
questions.solution:
• Incorrect Fact: It is built completely with marble.
  • Correction: Only the main dome is marble; the rest of the structure is encased in plaster and basalt.

questions.question: The Mahabodhi Temple was built entirely from ________ by Ashoka.
questions.solution:
• Mahabodhi Temple: bricks
  • Note: It is one of the oldest brick structures in India, marking the site where Buddha attained enlightenment.

questions.question: The entrance gateway in Dravidian style temple is known as:
questions.solution:
• Dravidian Gateway: Gopuram
  • Architecture: These are the monumental, often ornate towers at the entrance of South Indian temples.

questions.question: The Dhakeshwari Temple in present day Bangladesh has been constructed under the rule of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
• Dhakeshwari Temple: Sena
  • Founder: Tradition attributes it to Ballal Sen of the Sena dynasty in the 12th century.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first principal of the Bengal National College started in 1906?
questions.solution:
• First Principal: Aurobindo Ghose
  • Context: Founded during the Swadeshi Movement to provide national education free from British control.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements with regard to Satnami Movement of Central India.

a) The movement was founded by Ghasidas.

b) The movement was to improve the condition of leather workers.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Satnami Movement: Both a and b
  • Fact: Founded in the 1820s in Chhattisgarh. Ghasidas belonged to a leather-working caste and fought for social equality.

questions.question: In which year, and with what aim, was the Simon Commission appointed?
questions.option_1: In 1927, to recommend a further reform of India's Constitution
questions.option_2: In 1942, to enhance troop movements during the war
questions.option_4: In 1939, to evaluate India's war preparedness
questions.solution:
• Simon Commission: In 1927, to recommend a further reform of India's Constitution
  • Protest: It was boycotted because it had no Indian members ('All-White Commission').

questions.question: The Self-Respect movement was led by whom among the following social reformers?
questions.solution:
• Self-Respect Movement: EV Ramaswamy Naicker
  • Alias: Popularly known as 'Periyar', he started this movement in 1925 in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was the leader of which major peasant movement in 1928?
questions.solution:
• Bardoli Satyagraha: Bardoli Satyagraha
  • Patel's Title: The success of this no-tax campaign earned him the title 'Sardar' from the women of Bardoli.

questions.question: Who among the following was NOT one of the founders of the Ahrar Movement in British India?
questions.solution:
• Ahrar Movement Founder (NOT): Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
  • Note: Founded in 1910 by Mazhar-ul-Haq, Hakim Ajmal Khan, and Muhammad Ali.

questions.question: Khajuraho was one of the capitals of which of the following dynasties?
questions.solution:
• Khajuraho Capital: Chandela Dynasty
  • Temples: Built between 950 and 1050 CE, known for their Nagara-style architecture.

questions.question: Which of the following Government of India Acts of British India proposed the All India Federation (Federation of India)?
questions.solution:
• All India Federation: 1935
  • Act: The Government of India Act 1935 proposed a federation of British provinces and Princely States.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT including in the Pitt’s India Act of 1784?
questions.option_1: A committee of six government appointees, known as the Board of Control, was formed
questions.option_2: Madras and Bombay presidencies were brought under Bengal presidency
questions.option_3: All the debts of the East India Company were taken over by the British Government of India
questions.option_4: The governance of India was handed over to the Governor General and a council consisting of three members
questions.solution:
• Pitt’s India Act (NOT): All the debts of the East India Company were taken over by the British Government
  • Fact: The Act primarily established the Board of Control to supervise the Company's civil and military government.

questions.question: In which year did the government of British India pass a law according to which those who converted into Christianity got the right in their ancestral property?
questions.solution:
• Caste Disabilities Removal Act: 1850
  • Impact: It allowed converts to inherit ancestral property, which was seen as an attempt to encourage Christian conversions.

questions.question: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted in which year in British India to limit the freedom of the Indian-language press?
questions.solution:
• Vernacular Press Act: 1878
  • Viceroy: Enacted by Lord Lytton, it was known as the 'Gagging Act'.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts had provided the establishment of the Federal Court in British India?
questions.solution:
• Federal Court Act: The Government of India Act, 1935
  • History: It began functioning in 1937 and was the precursor to the Supreme Court of India.

questions.question: Which of the following sites would be suitable for observing the architecture of the Harappan civilisation?
questions.solution:
• Banawali: Banawali
  • Location: A major IVC site in Fatehabad, Haryana.

questions.question: The Aryans are considered to represent a linguistic group speaking which of the following groups of languages?
questions.solution:
• Aryan Language Group: Indo-European
  • Family: Specifically the Indo-Aryan branch of the Indo-Iranian family.

questions.question: Who built the Jaisalmer fort in 1156 AD?
questions.solution:
• Jaisalmer Fort: Rawal Jaisal
  • Fact: Known as the 'Golden Fort' (Sonar Kella) because of its yellow sandstone walls.

questions.question: ‘Senani’, ‘Kulapa’ and ‘Gramani’ are some of the functionaries mentioned primarily in which Veda?
questions.solution:
• Rigvedic Functionaries: Rigveda
  • Terms: Senani (Military chief), Kulapa (Head of family), Gramani (Village head).
